terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: ONE BAY of a modular outdoor roof kit, and the only one of the five whose ROOF SURFACE is real geometry: a 4 x 4 m cell on a 4 m grid, four whole-bamboo corner posts, and a roof of split culms laid alternately hollow-up and hollow-down as interlocking tiles. Nothing opens, turns or swings and nothing attaches -- a neighbouring bay is PLACED at 4 m, not socketed -- so one root pivot at base-center and zero sockets. Open on all four sides. Garden shelters, farm sheds, beach bars and temple fair stalls; the cheapest roof in the kit and the one a village builds itself. Culms weather from green through cream to grey and are tied, never nailed.

reasoning: ONE bamboo merge -- four posts, eight head rails on two levels, two king culms, the ridge pole, six rafters, the capping culm and sixteen lashing collars -- and ONE InstancedMesh of 33 four-culm PAIRS: TWO draw calls of 4, the cheapest submission count in the set.

The pair geometry carries FOUR culms -- channel and cap on the +Z slope and on the -Z slope -- so the instanced set varies in x alone and both slopes come off one geometry. Two sets, one per slope, would have been two draw calls and two geometries for the same triangles.

Two materials of three: bamboo (vertex colours -- two culm tones, rafter, rope, black cord) and split bamboo (WHITE, because setColorAt multiplies, with six tones carried per instance). Both textureless, each with one culm canvas.
The roof is 1,584 of the 2,552 triangles, which is the registry notes' own prediction that this module would sit nearest its ceiling. It is still 64% of the budget.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, no declared collider shape, no destruction groups.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the alternating half-pipe course, and the notes say so: a run of half-cylinders reads wrong when it is flat, because the silhouette at the eave is a scalloped edge and not a line. That scallop is 33 open culm mouths, and it is the one place in the set where triangles buy something a canvas cannot.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: The roof stops ON the module edge rather than overhanging it: a 4 m grid bay that overhangs collides with its neighbour.

The half-pipes are single-thickness SHELLS on a double-sided material, not walled tubes. A hollow-up channel is seen from the inside at every azimuth, and a real wall would triple the roof's triangles for 8 mm nobody resolves at prop distance; the scallop at the eave, which is what the notes actually ask for, is the shell's own open mouth.
Six segments per half culm. At a 118 mm pitch a culm is about 25 px across at prop distance, and the roof is 1,584 triangles at six; at twelve it would be 3,168 and over the ceiling with the frame.
The cap culm rides 62 mm above the channel plane and half a pitch across, which is how the two courses interlock; it is 55 mm radius against the channel's 50 so it bridges the gap.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 4.00 x 3.10 x 4.00 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=6 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; none collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The rigid body of the prop at its declared origin. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it, and only real mechanisms get one.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.
actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center, +Y up, the ridge along X. A neighbouring bay sits at +-4.00 m on X or Z with the same alignment, and the two bays' corner posts then pair at the shared edge.

silhouette.description: A 4.00 x 4.00 m bay: four 100 mm bamboo posts at the corners under a DOUBLE head rail at 2.02 and 2.24 m, a ridge pole on two king culms, six rafters, and a low gable of 33 pairs of split culms -- a hollow-up channel with a hollow-down cap riding on the two beside it -- from a 2.40 m eave to a 3.10 m capping culm. The eave is 33 open culm mouths, not a line. Open on all four sides.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x and z span -1.998..+1.998, set by the rope collars at the post heads: the post surface is already at 1.988 and a 66 mm collar radius crossed the cell edge at 2.004 on the first build, so the collars are 60 mm. y 0.000 to 3.100 at the crown of the capping culm -- which is r cos(PI/10) above its centre, not r, because a 10-segment cylinder has a flat there; centring it at H - r left the declared height 3.4 mm short. The roof culms were shortened 60 mm from the true rake: a cylinder rotated onto the slope has a z extent of half-L cos(s) + r sin(s), and at 40 mm short the cap culms reached 1.9974 against the frame collars' 1.9980 -- inside check-coplanar's 1 mm tolerance, and it reported all 66 pairs. On this bay the FRAME owns the z plane; on the two thatched ones the roof does. Proxy (Meshy v7): w:h:d 1 : 0.760 : 1.119, post grid 1.182 x 1.360 H, roof reaching 1.450 H at an eave sitting at 0.42 of the height -- a squat table of a shelter, which is what the plate shows. The notes fix a 2.40 eave under a 3.10 ridge, so the built bay is far taller in proportion and the roof is 23% of its height against the proxy's 58%. The proxy IS used for the culm diameter and for confirming the ridge runs across the narrow axis.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: w:h:d 1 : 0.760 : 1.119, post grid 1.182 x 1.360 H, roof 1.450 H, eave at 0.42 H, 39-degree pitch. Used for the culm diameter and for confirming the ridge axis. NOT used for the proportions: the plate is a squat stand-in and the notes fix a 4 x 4 m bay at 2.40/3.10.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.92: the bay is symmetric about both axes and open on all four sides; the plate shows one gable end and one full slope.

Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px CULM multiply canvas after construction with CULM UVs -- u around the circumference and v along the length, both in metres over 0.60, written per cylinder BEFORE its rotations. That is what puts two node rings on every pole at real spacing however the pole is turned; panel UVs would ring a post every 4 cm.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

localOverrides.evidence: crops/roofgreen.png and crops/roofcream.png, sd 38 and 41 -- the spread inside one crop IS the alternation; carried as six per-instance tones rather than as a texture.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-roofgreen (0.88) at #b0a78d sd 38 and region-roofcream (0.88) at #b9ab8f sd 41. The two means are close and the STANDARD DEVIATION is the finding: 38 to 41 inside a crop of one course means the roof is a mix of green, cream and weathered grey culms with no pattern, not two zones.

The material colour is WHITE, deliberately: InstancedMesh.setColorAt MULTIPLIES with material.color, so six tones ride on the instance colour attribute and a tinted base would ship all 33 pairs darkened by it. The tones are #b8bd9a, #cdc39c, #c3bda8, #c6c69e, #d2c8a2 and #bab7a2, assigned by k*5 mod 6 -- 5 and 6 are coprime, so it walks all six and never repeats within a cycle. The first build used (k*5 + k%3) % 6, which collapses to three clustered values and shipped 33 pairs of nearly one colour.
Authored a first time at a mean luma of 200 and MEASURED BACK at 188 on the up-facing slope against the plate's 163-169; pulled 7.5% and re-measured at 180 / 141 / 124 across the azimuths.
DOUBLE-SIDED, because a hollow-up channel is a single-thickness shell seen from the inside at every azimuth; without it half the roof is invisible.
Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px culm canvas with CULM UVs at 0.55 m, so the node rings cross each split culm at real spacing along its own length.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

repetitionSystems.name: Split bamboo half-pipe tiles
repetitionSystems.placement: 33 instances at a 118 mm pitch across x from -1.94 to 1.94. Each instance is FOUR half culms: on each slope a hollow-up channel (r 0.050) and a hollow-down cap (r 0.055) half a pitch across and 62 mm above it, both 2.057 m long on a 17.5 degree rake, six segments, open-ended, theta length PI. Six tones ride on the instance colour attribute.
repetitionSystems.notes: Both slopes are baked into the pair geometry so the set varies in x alone -- one draw call and one unique geometry for the whole roof. Which half of each shell is material follows from the rotation: rotateX(PI/2 + s) sends local +Z downward on the +Z slope, so a channel is theta start -PI/2 and a cap +PI/2, and the two swap on the -Z slope.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.87. 2,552/4,000 triangles, 2/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 2/6 unique geometries, two 512 px canvases. The roof is 62% of the triangles, which is what the registry notes predicted for this module. Open on all four sides and the eave is 33 open culm mouths: turntable with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement and a holeviz read per azimuth.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: One component plus one repetition system: 2 of 4, the cheapest submission count in the set.

materials.note: bamboo and split: 2 of 3. Two culm tones, the rafter, the rope and the black cord are vertex colours; the roof's six tones are per-instance.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 2,552 of 4,000: 968 in the frame merge (24 cylinders at 8 or 10 segments), 1,584 in 33 roof instances at 48 each (four six-segment open half culms). The roof is 62% of the model, which is the registry notes' own prediction for this module.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Cylinders throughout: closed for the frame poles, open partial cylinders (theta length PI) for the roof shells and the lashing collars.
One InstancedMesh of 33 four-culm pairs carrying both slopes. In a scene the HOST places whole bays on the 4 m grid.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Both materials are declared textureless. Two 512 px culm canvases after construction, ~2 MB of texture VRAM.

risks.description: The half-pipes are shells with no wall thickness, on a double-sided material.
risks.mitigation: A walled culm triples the roof's triangles for 8 mm nobody resolves at prop distance, and the scallop the notes ask for is the shell's own open mouth. Double-sided is not optional here: a hollow-up channel is seen from the inside at every azimuth.

risks.description: Six segments per half culm is coarse; at twelve the roof alone would be 3,168 triangles and over the ceiling with the frame.
risks.mitigation: At a 118 mm pitch a culm is about 25 px across at prop distance. Measured on the renders the course reads as round, and the budget verdict is 2,552 of 4,000.

risks.description: The proxy is a squat table with the eave at 0.42 H; the notes fix 2.40 under 3.10, which makes the roof 23% of the height against the proxy's 58%.
risks.mitigation: The notes are the module contract and the plate is a stand-in. The proxy IS used for the culm diameter and the ridge axis; arithmetic in envelopeDerivation.

risks.description: A 100 mm bamboo post is under the collider derivation's 0.15 m minimum rectangle, so the greedy cover took NO rectangle for the post layer and fell back to the mask's bounding box -- which for four corner posts is the whole 4 x 4 m bay. The first compound shipped a solid 4 x 4 x 1.84 m block under the roof, and promote refused it: 20% of the footprint standing more than the 0.30 m step height above the real surface, i.e. a player walking onto thin air at waist height inside a shelter whose whole purpose is to be walked under.
risks.mitigation: Fixed in scripts/lib/colliders.mjs rather than by thickening the posts, because 100 mm is the right culm: the fallback is now per CONNECTED COMPONENT when the bounding box is less than 35% full AND at least a square metre. Both conditions are measured -- splitting unconditionally dropped the soi dog from 0.973 to 0.718 coverage, because for four legs under a solid body the bbox IS the body. Re-derived all 122 existing compounds: four change part geometry (this bay, the stall cart, the songthaew and the tuk-tuk), none change coverage, and no shipped compound changes without a re-derive.

risks.description: Open on all four sides, and the eave is 33 open culm mouths, so a lot of what the silhouette encloses is background.
risks.mitigation: Turntable run with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement and a holeviz read per azimuth: the red covers the volume under the roof and the culm mouths, both genuine openings, and no solid surface. Every frame tone measured off the backdrop band first, darkest 77 against 58.
